author coordination mechanismOxygenated MWNT groups coordinate Cd precursor and seed in situ CdTe growth after Te solution injection. Nanotubes function as sterically bulky π-conjugated ligands and growth terminators.author derivedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 2, printed p. 10343, Coordination and synthesis rationale; banerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 7, printed p. 10348, Diffusion-limited growth; banerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 10349, Figure 8 and morphology discussion; banerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 9, printed p. 10350, Growth interpretation and conclusion
author ligand competition rationaleSubstoichiometric TDPA leaves some Cd available for surface coordination, especially through carboxylic acid/alcohol groups. No ligand-binding constant, available-site density or stoichiometric competition measurement is reported.author derivedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 2, printed p. 10343, Experimental Section, heterostructure synthesis
author diffusion limited shape mechanismA nanotube limits access to one crystal face; incoming monomer preferentially reaches the free end, producing pseudo-one-dimensional or anisotropic growth. This is a steric/diffusion interpretation, not a measured monomer-flux map.author derivedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 7, printed p. 10348, Growth-shape discussion
author shape variation factorsLocal group density, site geometry and spatial separation of groups on one tube or adjacent tubes can alter growth and the broad crystal size/shape range.author derivedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 10349, Morphology discussion
author tip growth rationaleGreater tip coverage is linked to curvature-induced reactivity and abundant oxygenated groups after cap opening/outer-wall etching. Aggressive oxidation also creates active sidewall sites.author derivedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 5, printed p. 10346, Microscopy discussion; banerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 6, printed p. 10347, Continuation
author intertube junction rationaleSpacing between tubes can allow growing crystals to bridge them, creating fused nanocrystal-mediated networks. Exact atomistic bonding, electronic coupling and carrier transport are not established from the static microscopy alone.author derivedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 2, printed p. 10343, Coordination and synthesis rationale; banerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 7, printed p. 10348, Diffusion-limited growth; banerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 10349, Figure 8 and morphology discussion; banerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 9, printed p. 10350, Growth interpretation and conclusion
figure8 schematic scopeFigure 8 schematically shows oxidation, Cd coordination/Te injection and in situ CdTe growth with probable multi-tube junction structures. TDPA ligands are omitted for clarity; the schematic is not measured atomic coordinates or a validated crystal model.reportedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 10349, Figure 8 caption
author passivation tradeoffBulky nanotubes cap limited surface regions, leaving incomplete passivation and possible surface oxidation during prolonged air exposure. Source TeO3 wording is retained; exposure kinetics and oxide identity are not independently resolved.author derivedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 10349, XPS interpretation
author swnt extension limitConventional oxidation of SWNTs has difficulty creating enough groups for dense QD growth without compromising tube structure/electronic integrity. This is qualitative extension context, not a fully specified current SWNT synthesis.reportedSource-reported observationstudybanerjee2003 · Main PDF p. 9, printed p. 10350, Conclusion
author future workFuture directions include charge transport through junctions, crystal growth across aligned nanotubes and thin composite films.
